title: Why Is the "Phygital" Shift Putting Immense Pressure on Store Associates?
summary: As modern retail evolves, leaders must strike a critical balance between customer convenience and margin protection.
body_markdown:
**


**Key Takeaways**


· Modern shoppers demand seamless omnichannel experiences. They expect to[Buy Online, Pick-Up In-Store (BOPIS)](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/resource-library/faq/What-is-Buy-Online,-Pick-Up-in-Store-BOPIS.html) , scan products on their phones in the aisle, and receive instant stock availability updates.


· Fragmented store systems force associates to work as cashiers and fulfillment coordinators so without real-time mobile tools, they waste valuable time walking between sales floors and back rooms just to check inventory.


· To win customer trust and loyalty, retailers must arm associates with connected mobility solutions that keep employees highly visible, accessible, and fully informed on the floor.


## How Does the Transition to GS1 Digital Link Transform Store Operations?


One of the biggest technological shifts on the retail horizon is the global transition from traditional 1D UPC barcodes to **2D**[GS1 Digital Link](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/cpn/implementing-gs1-digital-link.html) **** **barcodes.**


For decades, linear barcodes provided only a static product identifier.[2D barcodes](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/resource-library/faq/what-is-a-2d-barcode.html) unlock multidimensional data within a single, scannable code that facilitates:


· **Consumer Transparency:** Shoppers scan the code with a smartphone to see allergens, sustainability sourcing, and recipes.


· **Dynamic Markdown Management:** Associates scan the code at the shelf to track expiration dates and trigger automatic markdowns on expiring goods, dramatically reducing food waste.


·[Frictionless Checkout](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/resource-library/use-case-library/reducing-grocery-self-checkout-friction.html) **:** Cashiers and point-of-sale scanners read complex data instantly, speeding up transaction times.


Upgrading front-of-house scanners today ensures your stores are fully prepared for this global standard.


## How Can Computer Vision and Smart Scanning Protect Self-Checkout Margins?


While self-checkout provides speed and convenience, it has introduced significant vulnerability through[shrink](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/resource-library/use-case-library/protecting-high-value-merchandise-and-reducing-retail-shrink.html) , non-scanning, and fraudulent tag-switching.


Relying on store associates to manually police multiple self-checkout lanes is stressful for employees and creates uncomfortable interactions with honest customers. The solution is **smart**[computer vision](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/blog/posts/2026/edge-ai-to-stop-checkout-loss-at-point-of-sale.html) **embedded at the point of sale that provides:**


1. **Visual Item Recognition:** Integrated overhead cameras and intelligent scanner scales visually identify produce and merchandise.


2. **Real-Time Discrepancy Detection:** If a customer scans a low-cost item (like bananas) while bagging a premium product (like ribeye steak), the system flags the mismatch instantly before the transaction is completed.


3. **Targeted Intervention:** Alerts are sent discreetly to the attendant’s mobile computer, allowing them to assist without causing front-end friction.


## What Are the Next Steps for Modern Retail Leaders?


Succeeding in the connected store era requires striking a balance between customer convenience and margin protection. By arming frontline associates with mobile inventory intelligence, transitioning to 2D data-rich scanning, and safeguarding self-checkout with computer vision, retailers can design a modern store built to last.
